slides.title: What is Sexual Harassment?
slides.description: Definition: Sexual harassment refers to unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, and other verbal or physical conduct of a sexual nature.

slides.title: Types of Sexual Harassment
slides.description:
• Quid Pro Quo: When submission to or rejection of unwelcome sexual conduct is used as a basis for employment decisions (e.g., promotions, raises).
  • Hostile Work Environment: When unwelcome sexual behavior creates an intimidating, hostile, or offensive workplace.
  • Verbal Harassment: Unwanted comments, jokes, or questions about a person’s sex life or appearance.
  • Non-Verbal Harassment: Inappropriate gestures, sharing explicit images or videos, or leering.
  • Physical Harassment: Unwanted touching, blocking movements, or physically intimidating behavior.

slides.title: Recognizing Sexual Harassment
slides.description:
Signs to Look For:

  • Behavior that makes others uncomfortable or anxious.
  • Repeated unwanted advances, comments, or invitations.
  • Sexual comments or jokes that create a negative work environment.

slides.title: Impact of Sexual Harassment
slides.description:
• Effects on Individuals: Stress, anxiety, depression, decreased job satisfaction, and lower productivity.
  • Effects on the Organization: Legal liabilities, decreased morale, high turnover, and damage to reputation.

slides.title: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibits sexual harassment in the workplace.
slides.description:
• Employer’s Responsibility: Provide a safe work environment and respond promptly to complaints.
  • Employee Rights: Right to a harassment-free workplace and the right to report any incidents.

slides.title: What to Do If You Experience or Witness Sexual Harassment
slides.description:
Steps to Take:

  • Document the Incident: Write down dates, times, and details.
  • Report to HR or a Supervisor: Follow company procedures for reporting.
  • Seek Support: Talk to trusted colleagues or use external resources like hotlines.

slides.title: How to Prevent Sexual Harassment
slides.description:
Best Practices:

  • Create clear policies and communicate them to all employees.
  • Conduct regular training sessions on sexual harassment awareness.
  • Promote a culture of respect and zero tolerance for harassment.

slides.title: Reporting Mechanisms
slides.description:
• Internal Reporting: HR contacts, hotlines, or online reporting tools.
  • External Reporting: EEOC (Equal Employment Opportunity Commission) and legal options.
  • Protection from Retaliation: It’s illegal for employers to retaliate against someone for reporting harassment.

slides.title: Role of Managers and Supervisors
slides.description:
Responsibilities:

  • Respond to complaints promptly and confidentially.
  • Ensure no retaliation occurs.
  • Set a positive example by treating all employees with respect.

slides.title: Creating a Respectful Workplace
slides.description:
• Promote Inclusion and Diversity: Encourage a workplace culture that values all individuals.
  • Encourage Open Communication: Create safe spaces for employees to express concerns.
  • Lead by Example: Show respect in every interaction, at every level.

questions.question: Sexual harassment only includes physical actions, such as unwanted touching
Which of the following is an example of quid pro quo sexual harassment?

answers.a: A supervisor offering a promotion in exchange for a date.
answers.b: A coworker telling jokes about their weekend plans.
answers.c: An employee asking another employee to lunch.
answers.d: A colleague complimenting a new hairstyle.

questions.question: It is illegal for an employer to retaliate against an employee who reports sexual harassment.
Which of the following behaviors could create a hostile work environment?

answers.a: Regularly making unwanted sexual comments or jokes.
answers.b: Discussing work projects with a coworker.
answers.d: Offering feedback during a performance review.

questions.question: Reporting sexual harassment to HR is the only option available for an employee who experiences harassment.
